findings.claim: The shipped game uses 76 distinct map centres across 81 stock mission files. These come from stock missions plus 3 stock campaigns. The stock InstantActionConfig.ini has no MapCenter at all, and Instant Action is disabled. The centres span lat -45.91 to 82.08 and lon -132.5 to 175.48. They concentrate in the Norwegian Sea/GIUK (12), the Mediterranean (9), the Norwegian coast (7), Philippines/Sulu/Borneo (7) and the Persian Gulf (5), with 4 each in Taiwan/East China Sea/Okinawa, the South China Sea and Indonesia.

findings.claim: Coverage of the project regions by stock content is uneven. That reflects what the game ships, not a limit. Stock missions put units within ~60 nm of Guam, Hainan/Yulin, Kola, Petropavlovsk, Bodø, Diego Garcia, Souda and Djibouti. They come within 90-260 nm of the East China Sea, Bahrain and Darwin. No stock mission puts a unit within 500 nm of San Diego (763 nm), Norfolk (894), Pearl Harbor (1,512), Yokosuka (610), Stirling (741), Brest (658) or Mount Pleasant/Falklands (3,634). Stock world-data nodes do exist at San Diego, Norfolk, Honolulu, Yokohama, Perth, Darwin, Brest, Vladivostok, Petropavlovsk and Severomorsk. The Falklands have no stock node within 959 nm, though a Falklands terrain biome exists.
findings.evidence: Nearest-point computation over 2,345 decoded stock unit placements (RelativePositionInNM decoded as lat=clat+z/60, lon=clon+x/60, plus GeoPosition) and 1,038 Location= nodes in mods-source/_vanilla/original/campaigns/*.ini. Nodes found: us_cities_pacific.ini San Diego and Honolulu, us_ports_atlantic.ini Port Norfolk, asia_ports.ini Yokohama, oceania_cities.ini Perth and Darwin, cities.ini 'Brest Fr' and Bodo, soviet_ports_east.ini Vladivostok and Petropavlovsk, soviet_cities_west.ini Severomorsk. Nearest Falklands node: sea_points.ini 'Rio de la Plata', 959 nm. terrain/biomes.ini:5 Biome3=Falklands.

findings.claim: RelativePositionInNM is a flat plate-carree encoding. x = delta-longitude x 60 (minutes of longitude, with no cos(lat) correction). z = delta-latitude x 60, with positive z pointing NORTH. The stock documentation gets z the wrong way round and calls x 'miles'. At 69°N one x unit is only ~0.36 nm on the ground.
findings.evidence: Texas twin missions: the same land unit wp_cross_slot differs by exactly dx=3669.00, dz=-1143.00. That equals 61.15° x 60 and -19.05° x 60 between missions/NATO/Don't Mess With Texas (Blue Side).ini:110-111 (centre 35.22,34.87) and missions/Warsaw Pact/Don't Mess With Texas (Red Side).ini:33-34 (centre 54.27,-26.28; unit at :72). Stock airfields decode with z positive north onto real fields: Warsaw Pact/Breakthrough.ini Taskforce2LandUnit2 (-9.7,-6.0) -> 36.160,-5.352 (Gibraltar); NATO/Caron at Grenada 1983.ini NeutralLandUnit1 -> 12.002,-61.772 (Point Salines); NATO/Showdown off Guam Blue 1985.ini Taskforce1LandUnit1 (172.5,-194.28) -> 13.592,144.935 (Andersen; z-positive-south would give 20.07N, open sea). ui/minimap.ini:15 says 'one degree is 60nm'. changelog.txt:2618 refers to 'our flat Earth'. Contradicting stock doc: missions/Demo/MissionFileInformation.ini:443 '#negative values go west for x and north for z' and :447 'offset in miles'.

findings.claim: Shipped, maintained stock missions show that the map centre does not bound unit placement. Three use centre 54.27,-26.28 (mid-North Atlantic) and place every unit 3,900-12,160 nm away, where the action actually happens.

One Aegean mission spawns Yak-38s in the Barents Sea. Typical stock missions are much smaller: median spawn span 193 nm, or 330 nm including waypoints.

findings.claim: The game's only statement about what the centre does is a performance recommendation plus a local-time reference. It is not a bound. No stock UI string mentions map edges, placement bounds, theatre or region selection, or unit-count caps.
findings.evidence: language_en/ui.ini:1256 'CentralMapPointTooltip=Sets the coordinates of the mission's central map point - drag this to the center of the scenario for best performance - also used to calculate the Local time'. ui.ini:1255 LocalTimeTooltip ('local time at the mission center point'). MissionFileInformation.ini:148 '#Map location. Use real world coordinates for mission area central position'. A grep of ui.ini for too many / out of bounds / off map / edge / exceed / limit finds only air-ops, sea-state and fleet-points caps (ui.ini:401, 422, 2009, 3652, 4650) and RebaseTooFar (4159, aircraft range).

findings.claim: The engine moves its Unity-space origin during play, using 'relocation events' around a 'center tile' (a floating-origin scheme). The mission's MapCenter is therefore not a permanent rendering origin. Relocation has had bugs.
findings.evidence: changelog.txt:4380 (0.1.1.2 #123, 16-Jan-2025): 'terrain at 180° E/W where the center tile was calculated wrongly and led to a relocation loop (still WIP)'. :4793 (0.1.0.6, 30-Nov-2024): ASROC misbehaved 'in case of a relocation event'. :5099 (#74, 12-Nov-2024): 'cascade of endless further relocation events'. :4030 (0.1.1.5): 'Dead units were teleported due to malfunction in relocation handling'. :2882 (0.4.3, 16-Aug-2025): 'Autogen buildings jumping during relocation and camera jump'. :3482: 'Weapons relocation on save load'. :5647; :2236 (0.6.8): 'Ghost objects at world origin'. That relocation exists is high confidence; that it is a full floating origin is an inference (medium).

findings.claim: The ±180° date line is the edge of the engine's flat-Earth frame and a documented bug area. No stock mission places units across it, yet the Pacific project regions (Hawaii, Midway, Guam, Kamchatka) sit near it.
findings.evidence: changelog.txt:2618-2619 (0.5.0 #235, 01-Oct-2025): 'Huge calculation error for units at date line "edge" of our flat Earth (pun intended!)' and 'Some out of bounds longitude positioning when crossing the date line "border"'. :4096 (0.1.1.4, 17-Feb-2025): 'Trial of fix for 180° E/W location'. :4380: relocation loop at 180° 'still WIP'. A scan of all 81 stock files found zero unit positions with decoded lon beyond ±180. campaigns/airports.ini includes PMDY Midway (-177.38) and PJON (-169.53). Behaviour in 0.8.4 has not been tested.

findings.claim: The mission format also supports absolute GeoPosition, and saves store geo-positions rather than Unity coordinates. Relative nautical miles are only one of two representations.
findings.evidence: MissionFileInformation.ini:436-440 '#0) Geo position. Direct position definition <latitude, longitude, altitude>' (GeoPosition=38.0753,21.9964,3392). Used in stock: NATO/Hormuz.ini:158, Hormuz_hard.ini:193, Hormuz_tarawa.ini:193, Don't Mess With Texas (Blue Side).ini:159 and (Red Side).ini:80. changelog.txt:5348 (#68, 26-Oct-2024) 'Mission Editor: GeoPosition support on unit loading'. :2485 (0.5.3 #250, 13-Nov-2025): towed-trail positions 'were saved in Unity coordinates ... changed to Geopositions'. :4409: AimPointGeoPosition. config.ini:7-8 SaveLoadEnabled=True, SaveLoadSensorDataEnabled=True.

findings.claim: Terrain, clouds and autogen are streamed in camera-local chunks. No stock config defines a world or map extent. These settings say nothing about the simulation cost of distant active units.
findings.evidence: terrain/terrain.ini:16 MaxParallelLoadingJobs=32; :20 ChunksViewDistance=4. clouds.ini:39 'CloudCullingDistance=4 // culling distance in chunks, where one chunk is about 50km wide'. config.ini [AutoGen] Level6 MaxDrawRange=1000. ui/Default/Settings_UI_Tactical.ini:105 MapSize=400,400 is the on-screen widget size, not the world. changelog.txt:3873 (0.1.1.8 #149, 18-Mar-2025) 'Major overhaul of terrain system and map'; :3870 terrain loading performance; :2200 VRAM spikes 'during eg biome crossing'.

findings.claim: Terrain uses a global biome scheme, and changelog fixes refer to specific places worldwide. The heightmap data is not in the repo, so actual terrain coverage and quality at each project location are unverified. The one stated placement rule is that land units must sit at least 1 m above sea level.

findings.claim: Time compression is capped at 100x by a config value, and the engine also limits compression on its own during engagements and for some weapon types. At 100x, one game day takes 14.4 real minutes, and a 2,000 nm transit at 20 kt (100 game hours) takes about 60 real minutes.
findings.evidence: config.ini:13 MaxTimeCompression=100. changelog.txt:5344 (#68, 26-Oct-2024) 'Setting max time compression to 100'; :5664 'Setting for max time compression'; :5121 (#74) 'Limited time compression for engagements'; :5104 sonobuoys limited; :5022 rebalanced limits for gun and CIWS; :4065 missile group and weapon limit; :5694 performance under time acceleration. The transit figures are plain arithmetic, not measured.

findings.claim: The largest stock mission has 130 units. No stock config key or string declares a unit cap. The changelog treats unit and formation count as a performance cost and ships fixes for it. The stock maximum is an example, not a limit.
findings.evidence: Summed NumberOf* counts: NATO/Red Madagascar 1985.ini 130; pacific-strike 09 Shadows off Palawan 86; 08 Defense of North Borneo 76; NATO/Dangerous Straits 1985 71. Largest stock mission file is 63 KB. changelog.txt:2275-2278 (0.6.8 #265, 17-Dec-2025): 'Drastically improved mission loading times', 'Reworked sensor and line of sight logic to improve performance', 'Improved performance with large formations'. :65-67 (0.8.2, 28-Sep-2026) performance updates. config.ini:3 EnablePerformanceLogging=False is a built-in measurement hook (changelog.txt:5302). MissionFileInformation.ini:7-10 '//DisableTerrain=False' is a per-mission debug switch.

findings.claim: Stock's only shipped way to play persistently across regions is a linear campaign of separate missions. Losses, ammunition and a tracked theatre order of battle (ORBAT) carry over between missions, with resupply and repair available. This shows what the game ships. It is not evidence that such a split is required.
findings.evidence: campaigns/strike-group-molniya-campaign/campaign.ini:5 Type=Linear; :9 [PersistentData]; :21 'This is a persistent campaign. Ship/aircraft losses and weapon expenditures are tracked, and will carry forward across each mission. Resupply is available at certain points'. Its missions use 5 different centres, from -11.53,0.27 to 8.69,74.56. campaigns/pacific-strike-task-force/enemy_theater_roster.ini:3 'updates the campaign savefile with the theater ORBAT as ships are destroyed' and :8 persistent units tracked. changelog.txt:1805 'Linear persistent campaign Molniya'; :1807 CampaignRearm/CampaignRepair/CampaignResetAirgroup flags; :1046 rearm and repair trigger actions; :44 (0.8.x) 'Fixed campaign persistence for units sometimes not working'.

findings.claim: Stock ships a global node-and-link world dataset (ports, airports, sea points and links, patrol areas). It also ships a prototype theatre-wide campaign, spanning the US East Coast to Murmansk and Havana, that uses this data with no MapCenter at all. The sea network covers the Atlantic, Mediterranean and western Indian Ocean only; airports reach Hawaii, Guam, Kamchatka and Midway.
findings.evidence: campaigns/campaign-proto-1/campaign.ini:1-15 (BackgroundTraffic=Hidden, PortsFiles, SeaPointsFiles, SeaLinksFiles, AirportsFiles, PatrolAreasFiles, CitiesFiles, LandLinksFiles); :18-19 'Campaign Prototype 1 / A test of the text parsing system'. Groups at Port Norfolk, New London, Charleston, Mayport and Holy Loch versus Port Murmansk, Severodvinsk and Havana (lines 33-196). sea_points.ini: 431 points, lat -36.05..76.54, lon -87.47..61.16. sea_links.ini: 1,062 sections. airports.ini: 48 airports, lon -177.38..167.73 (PHIK Hickam, PGUA Andersen, RODN Kadena, UHPP Elizovo, PMDY Midway). patrol_areas.ini: 51 areas. changelog.txt:3967 'City view popup in Dynamic Campaign'. config.ini:5 CampaignEnabled=True.

findings.claim: Background data (LoadBackgroundData) attaches world-spanning files to single stock missions. A Norway mission, for example, loads all 48 airports from Heathrow to Hickam and Midway. The data cannot show whether the engine actually creates every distant entry or filters them by distance.

MissionFileInformation.ini:742-744 'Loads land units from files listed in [BackgroundData]'. ui.ini:141 'background data that is loaded on startup'. changelog.txt:3161 'Background scenery was misplaced due to wrong geo center position at time of creation'.

findings.claim: 54.27,-26.28 is very likely the in-game Mission Editor's default centre. The player's own editor-made NORTHERN FRONT.ini keeps that centre and places 288 units 9,000-12,000 nm away in the Banda/Arafura/northern Australia area. Those positions decode exactly onto the real RAAF bases.
findings.evidence: 3 stock missions and 237 of the 394 .ini files under mods-source/_vanilla/user/missions use exactly 54.27,-26.28. No stock config file contains the value (grep). mods-source/_vanilla/user/missions/NORTHERN FRONT.ini:65-66 sets the centre. Decoded: Taskforce1LandUnit1 airbase_raaf_darwin -> -12.427,130.884; LandUnit5 airbase_raaf_scherger -> -12.603,142.038; LandUnit9 airbase_raaf_townsville -> -19.253,146.765. All placements fall within lat -23.76..3.53 and lon 103.44..165.91. That it is the editor default is an inference; whether this mission played correctly is outside this lens.

findings.claim: The SEST builders use the same plate-carree convention as the game, so the coordinate conversion adds no extent limit of its own. Builder snapping is a separate, builder-only constraint: build_pack.py snaps or refuses coastal stations unless an earlier mission placed a unit nearby. Regions with no stock or SEST placements (Hawaii, the US coasts, Brest, the Falklands) are therefore a builder data gap, not an engine limit.
findings.evidence: integration/missions/build_land_defence.py:772 '# Geometry: x = minutes of longitude, z = minutes of latitude', with cos(lat) handling at :779-799. integration/missions/build_northern_front_ii.py:44-48 (x=(lon-MLON)*60, 'verified against Darwin/Scherger'). integration/campaign/build_pack.py:751-754 POOL_ROOTS = integration/missions, _vanilla/original/missions, _vanilla/original/campaigns, _vanilla/user/missions; :825 OFFSHORE_SNAP=8.0; :828 OPEN_SEA=25.0; :929-970 open_water() refuses any station within 25 nm of known land and more than 8 nm from proven water ('Move it, or mark the station coastal=True'). docs/campaigns/southern-watch/build-notes.md:1250-1258 (~5,300 proven points).

findings.claim: Nothing in the stock data, UI strings or the 5,736-line changelog states a maximum playable extent, a maximum distance from the centre, a requirement for separate regional missions, or a unit cap. The quantities that would actually limit a single populated world remain unmeasured: per-unit simulation cost for hundreds of active units far from the camera, save size and reload time, how often time compression is auto-limited at scale, and date-line behaviour in 0.8.4.
findings.evidence: Negative greps over language_en/ui.ini, config.ini, terrain/*.ini, clouds.ini, camera.ini, ui/*.ini and changelog.txt for extent, bounds, edge, unit-limit and theatre-limit wording (hits listed in the other findings). The largest stock mission has 130 units. The one SEST mission at 974 units (mods-source/_vanilla/user/missions/user_missions/SEST Indo-Pacific Land Assets.ini, centre -6,130, max offset 1,815 nm) is builder output whose runtime behaviour is not recorded in stock data.

open_questions: Does the centre's location measurably matter (ui.ini:1256 'for best performance')? The stock Texas twins are a ready-made A/B test: the same units with centre near the action (Blue, 35.22,34.87) versus 3,900 nm away (Red, 54.27,-26.28). Compare load time, frame time, placement accuracy and AI behaviour.
Is the date-line problem (changelog.txt:2618-2619, 4096, 4380) fully fixed in 0.8.4? Test units, waypoints and camera moves crossing ±180° near Midway or the Aleutians, and a save/reload taken there.

How do frame time, load time, save size and reload time scale at 130, 300 and 1,000 concurrently active units spread over several thousand nm? Use config.ini EnablePerformanceLogging=True, and MissionFileInformation.ini DisableTerrain to separate terrain cost from simulation cost.
Does LoadBackgroundData create every global airport, city and port entry (e.g. Hickam in a Norway mission) or filter them by distance? This changes the cost of a world-wide background layer.
Does raising MaxTimeCompression above 100 in the user config take effect? How often does the engine's engagement auto-limit (changelog.txt:5121) cap compression in a busy, populated world?

What terrain heightmap coverage and quality exist at the regions with no stock content (Falklands/Mount Pleasant, Diego Garcia, Stirling, Pearl Harbor, San Diego, Norfolk, Brest)? The heightmaps are not in the repo.
Confirm 54.27,-26.28 is the Mission Editor's default centre by creating a new mission in-game.

Is there a polar clamp? The highest stock placement is 85.05°N (Northern Passage Tu-95, 407.98,30000,178.3 from 82.08,15.03), right at the Web-Mercator limit of 85.0511°. This is not relevant to the current regions (max ~71°N).
The stock doc (MissionFileInformation.ini:443) says negative z is north, but the data show positive z is north. Check that no SEST tool or handoff document has copied the stock doc's sign.

findings.claim: The map centre does not cap how far units can be from it: the engine has loaded, run and saved missions whose units are all 9,000 to 11,900 file units from the centre. NORTHERN FRONT III FINAL (centre 54.27,-26.28 in the North Atlantic; units at lat -24 to 10, lon 103 to 166) was played from 12:00 to 18:53 game time and saved mid-game.
findings.evidence: Save: data/install-snapshot/saves/New midgame.sav, Name=NORTHERN FRONT III FINAL (line 12), Time=18,53 (line 69). Mission start: integration/missions/NORTHERN FRONT III FINAL.ini:60 Time=12,0. The save is 22.8 MB and holds 298 units (65 land, 91 vessels, 6 subs, 100 airborne aircraft, 21 helos, 15 biologics) plus 30 weapons in flight, with GeoPositions spanning lat -21.22..10.39, lon 106.07..163.07. Second save: NORTHERN FRONT MIDGAME III.sav, Name=NORTHERN FRONT II, Time=12,36 against a mission start of 12,0 (NORTHERN FRONT II.ini:34); 14.0 MB, 206 units. findings.claim: RelativePositionInNM is stored by the engine as arcminutes on both axes, not as nautical miles east-west: lat = MapCenterLatitude + z/60 and lon = MapCenterLongitude + x/60. The stock reference file calls the format '<nmi,feet,nmi>', but the game's own save shows plain arcminutes. So a file 'x' is a longitude offset, and file-plane distances are not real distances away from the equator.
findings.evidence: Game-written save NORTHERN FRONT MIDGAME III.sav:173 has Taskforce1LandUnit1 GeoPosition=-12.426668081751,130.884157382087. The player's editor save (git show daedda0e:'mods-source/_vanilla/user/missions/NORTHERN FRONT.ini', airbase_us) has RelativePositionInNM=9429.85,low,-4001.8 with centre 54.27,-26.28. Check: 54.27 - 4001.8/60 = -12.42667 and -26.28 + 9429.85/60 = 130.88417. Across all land units with matching index and type (NF II as committed before the save, 49ddd405): 7 match to under 0.01 arcmin and 10 formation members to under 0.5 arcmin. A true-NM reading at the centre latitude would put Darwin at lon -117. Stock doc: mods-source/_vanilla/original/missions/Demo/MissionFileInformation.ini:443,448. The game changelog calls the world 'our flat Earth' (mods-source/_vanilla/changelog.txt:2618, 0.5.0). The builder uses the same convention: integration/campaign/build_pack.py:770-773 and integration/missions/build_northern_front_ii.py:47-51.

Three stock missions use centre 54.27,-26.28 while their units are in the NW Pacific, the Yucatan Strait and off Syria; their Blue-side twins use local centres. The centre is an arbitrary origin in shipped content.

findings.claim: In practice 54.27,-26.28 is the mission editor's default origin, used by several independent authors. 173 of the 502 distinct mission files use it, and in every one of them every placed unit is more than 1,000 file units from it.

Independent editor output: Workshop 3491248180 shipped its editor files missions/_Custom Mission.ini:25-26 and missions/_temp/_TempMission.ini with this centre and units in the Saronic Gulf (lat 37.55..37.99); its 'Lighting Strike' missions use it with units at 69-70N. findings.claim: The engine uses a moving origin ('relocation events') and a streaming terrain loader with a centre tile. MapCenter is the file's coordinate datum, not a fixed physics origin. The changelog says nothing about what triggers a relocation or whether there is a distance limit.

findings.claim: The date line (±180°) is the edge of the engine's flat world and has needed repeated fixes. The only repo mission that straddles it writes its western cluster about 21,500 file units east rather than about 60 west, so file coordinates do not wrap. Whether the engine joins the two clusters at runtime is not measured. This matters for any single-origin Hawaii to Guam/Japan layout.
findings.evidence: Changelog lines 2618-2619 (0.5.0, 01-Oct-2025): 'Huge calculation error for units at date line "edge" of our flat Earth', 'out of bounds longitude positioning when crossing the date line "border"'. It is plain arcminutes on both axes: lat = MapCenterLatitude + z/60 and lon = MapCenterLongitude + x/60. One x unit is cos(lat) NM east-west (0.36 NM at 69N, 0.14 NM at 82N). The map centre is only the origin of this lat/lon offset, not a local flat frame with a size.

The committed geo/southern_theatre_coast.json has box [100,-72,180,-25], 111 rings, 12,167 points and 241 KB. In Natural Earth 1:10m, Diego Garcia is a single 27-point polygon with 0 holes (scratch check), so a ship in the lagoon reads on_land=True. findings.claim: build_pack.py's main distance function, nm_between, is a flat-earth (mean-latitude) approximation with no longitude wrap. It is accurate within a theatre but wrong across the antimeridian. coast.py's index has the same no-wrap assumption.
findings.evidence: build_pack.py:816-819. Similar flat formulas are at coast.py:66-77 and briefing_maps.py:233-235. Compared with great-circle distance (scratch): Severomorsk-Evenes 365 vs 364 NM, Diego Garcia-Djibouti 2,090 vs 2,083, Norfolk-Brest 3,241 vs 3,122 (+3.8%). Across the antimeridian: Guam-Pearl 17,333 vs 3,303 (+425%) and Yelizovo-Pearl 15,230 vs 2,754 (+453%). The coast.py cell keys at :40-44 and :82 are floor(lon/0.5), with no modulo, so cells either side of 180 are not neighbours.

findings.claim: Sixteen distance and bearing checks in build_pack.py use raw x/z values as if x were NM east. But x is arcminutes of longitude, so these checks overstate east-west distance by 1/cos(lat) and skew bearings at mid and high latitudes. They also break across the antimeridian. This is a builder defect that can be fixed by converting to lat/lon and using great-circle distance; it is not an engine limit.
findings.evidence: The docstring at build_pack.py:2453-2457 (_bearing) says 'in the mission's NM frame: x east, z north', which contradicts the builder's own datum at :770-774 and :1594-1595. math.hypot over x/z is used at :1791 (airliner path length), :1891 (home-base reach), :2561/2569/2580-2581/2708-2709/2737 (protection and closure), :2864/2877/2891/2907 (victory reachability), :3719 (lift circle vs radius NM) and :4891 (sortie radius). The overstatement factor is x1.02 at 12S, x1.35 at 42S (Southern Reach), x1.49 at 48N (Brest), x2.00 at 60N (Bergen) and x2.79 at 69N (Kola). Examples: Severomorsk-Evenes measures 1,005 NM in x/z against 364 true; Norfolk-Brest 4,361 against 3,122 (scratch).

findings.claim: The builder's civil 'airway' generator extends the route in a straight lat/lon line by a factor proportional to the mission clock, with no clamp. That works for 45-75 minute missions but sends waypoints past the poles or around the globe under a long persistent clock.
findings.evidence: build_pack.py:1606-1617: stretch = max(1, AIRWAY_MARGIN * civil_reach_nm(mission) / dist), and route=(lat + (to_lat-lat)*stretch, ...). civil_reach_nm is at :813 (470 kn * minutes/60). campaign_data.py:524/662/810/936/1052 set minutes=45-75. Worked example: Darwin to Singapore under a 1,440-minute clock gives stretch about 9.3, which puts the waypoint at lat about 116 (off the globe).

findings.claim: The tooling already has a global land/water source: global_land_mask, a worldwide 1 km mask used by the mission-level tools. Only build_pack.py relies on the regional pool or extract. The sea-lane router builds its grid from the via points' bounding box with no wrap, so lanes across the antimeridian cannot be routed.
findings.evidence: global_land_mask is used by integration/missions/fix_land_positions.py:31-45, thin_waypoints.py:41,79, build_land_defence.py:74,805, build_indo_pacific_showcase.py:483-486 and sea_routes.py:31-34. It is not installed in this container. sea_routes.py:155-160 grid_for uses box = floor(min(lon)-pad) .. ceil(max(lon)+pad), with STEP=0.025 deg (:36). For Guam to Pearl that box spans 311 degrees the wrong way round within a narrow latitude band, which ends in 'no water path' SystemExit at :172-173. build_land_defence.py:780-798 (Geo) is the one helper that correctly scales east-west offsets by cos(lat) on the arcminute datum.

findings.claim: No SEST builder or checker enforces a maximum distance from the map centre, and the validation tools contain no spatial limits. The builder's split into short missions, each with its own centre, is a design choice, not a response to a measured engine limit.
findings.evidence: build_pack.py writes MapCenter verbatim from mission['centre'] (:3211) and positions as (lon-centre)*60 (:1594-1595, :1703-1705), with no range check (grep of all 'centre' uses). campaign_data.py gives each mission a centre and a 45-75 minute clock. tools/check_scenarios.py:12-17 checks counts, formations, duplicate sections and formation counts only. tools/preflight.py:17-23 checks references only. make_scenarios.py:3-6 carves NORTHERN FRONT III because it is 'heavy for a quick fight', a design judgment, and :18-19 notes 'Positions are absolute'.

findings.claim: The briefing-map generator cannot usefully draw a global mission: it is a plate carrée box around every unit, with an Indo-Pacific default inset, a fixed 50/100 NM scale bar and no antimeridian handling. This is a cosmetic builder limit. The game can generate its own briefing-map start view from the editor centre and zoom.
findings.evidence: integration/missions/briefing_maps.py:10 (datum), :171-190 extent() (min/max lon, no wrap), :295 (graticule step 1 or 2 degrees), :342 (default inset (93,-26,162,14)), :434-436 (scale bar 50/100 NM), and :262-283 off_chart (focus_nm). Game side: ui.ini:704.

findings.claim: The campaign builder's output paths are fixed to the published SEST_Campaign pack and rewrite pack-level files on every build. Reusing build_pack.py for the world sandbox as-is would change published content.

findings.claim: No performance figure exists in the repo for large or far-flung missions: no load times, frame rates or unit-count ceilings. SEST unit densities were deliberately kept low pending profiling. Any statement about active-world capacity is currently unmeasured.

The largest mission evidence is NORTHERN FRONT III (about 260-293 units, 70-81 KB) with 14-23 MB saves; no timing was recorded.

open_questions: Performance vs centre offset: the game's tooltip says to drag the centre to the scenario 'for best performance' (ui.ini:1256). How big is that effect? Test: load the same unit set with the centre over the action and then 2,000, 5,000 and 8,000 NM away, recording load time, frame rate at 1x and 20x, and Player.log.

Antimeridian behaviour (no repo mission has crossed it): do units at 179.9E and 179.9W spawn correctly? Does a ship given a waypoint across 180 take the short way or travel x/z the long way round? Does the 'relocation loop' from changelog:4380 recur in 0.8.4?

How does the game measure distance in an area trigger (Condition AreaRadiusNM) and in RandomSpawnRange or formation spacing 'in miles' at high latitude: true NM or x/z units? The builder's lift-circle check (build_pack.py:3719) assumes x/z units.

Waypoint pathing over long legs: does the engine follow a great-circle, a rhumb line, or a straight x/z line, for example Norfolk to Brest or Guam to Yokosuka? This decides whether builder route math must be great-circle.

Active-unit capacity: frame rate and simulation cost against the number of simultaneously active units spread across many regions, compared with NORTHERN FRONT III's ~260-293 units concentrated in one region. Does dormant or distant content cost anything (relocation events, terrain chunks under ChunksViewDistance=4)?

Save and reload at global extent: does a save with units in several hemispheres reload with positions, ammunition and Task Force Mode state intact? Saves store GeoPosition, but the multi-region case is untested.

Does the game's 1 km terrain show water where Natural Earth 1:10m shows land (Diego Garcia lagoon, Hood Canal/Kitsap, Kola Bay)? Needs a spawn test at those anchorages before trusting either the coastline extract or the global_land_mask check.
Is 54.27,-26.28 the editor's default map centre? 237 user missions use it, but the value is not found in any stock config.

Should the world builder use GeoPosition for absolute placement, which stock syntax supports (MissionFileInformation.ini:436-440)? That would avoid centre-relative arithmetic entirely; it needs one in-game confirmation that GeoPosition works for every unit class (vessels, submarines, aircraft and land units).

Builder decisions to make before a global build: replace pool snapping with the global coastline extract or global_land_mask, switch the 16 x/z hypot sites and nm_between to great-circle on lat/lon with longitude wrap, clamp airway stretch for long clocks, and give a world builder its own output root outside integration/campaign/SEST_Campaign.

The player's NORTHERN FRONT missions set the centre in the North Atlantic (54.27N, 26.28W), while every unit is in northern Australia, Indonesia and PNG. The mid-mission save holds 298 placed units (251 moving faster than 1 kt), 634 aircraft in custom air groups, 30 weapons in flight and an airstrike in progress. findings.claim: RelativePositionInNM is a coordinate representation that maps linearly to degrees: lat = centre + z/60 and lon = centre + x/60, with no cos(latitude) factor. Positions the engine itself wrote reproduce this exactly at offsets of about 10,000. The x value is therefore arc-minutes of longitude rather than true nautical miles away from the equator; at 69N one x unit is about 0.36 NM. The builder uses the same formula.

Scherger checks the same way: .ini:2145 10099.11,low,-4012.38 against .sav:496 -12.60299,142.03848. The builder's formula is in docs/campaigns/southern-watch/build-notes.md:1256 ('checked against the two RAAF bases ... within a mile'). This does not show whether the simulation uses flat or spherical geometry for distances.

open_questions: How long does a mission load, and at what frame rate and sim rate does it run, on the player's PC (RTX 2070 SUPER, 8 GB VRAM; CPU and RAM unknown)? Test NORTHERN FRONT III FINAL (about 270 placed units plus about 545 based aircraft), SEST Banda Front EDITED (857) and SEST Indo-Pacific Land Assets (974). Use a stopwatch plus config.ini EnablePerformanceLogging=True, which has never been tried.
Do 'New midgame.sav' (22.8 MB, 298 units) and 'NORTHERN FRONT MIDGAME III.sav' still reload on 0.8.4 Build 261002, how long does it take, and do aircraft, airstrikes and in-flight weapons survive?

Does one mission with units on both sides of 180 degrees (for example Pearl Harbor at 158W and Guam at 145E) load, render terrain, route ships and aircraft, and save and reload correctly on 0.8.4? The changelog's date-line fixes are historical, and the repo has no test.

Does the engine cap time compression for the whole mission when an engagement, gunfire or sonobuoys are active in any one region? What compression can a mission with about 300 moving units sustain at 8x, 20x and 100x?

What does a map centre far from the action cost? The developer tooltip says centre it 'for best performance'. A test could run the same NORTHERN FRONT III with its centre at 54.27,-26.28 and at about -10,130.

Because longitude maps linearly (x/60 degrees, no cos-lat factor) on what the changelog calls a 'flat Earth', are speeds, sensor ranges and weapon ranges distorted east-west at high latitudes (Kola and Barents at about 69N, the Falklands at 52S)? A ship's measured east-west transit at 69N would settle it.
Which mission hung on load on 20 Sep 2026, and was the Nimitz (2000s) Variant3 override really the cause? It is still withheld and unproven.

How much frame and tick time do the installed code mods (CV16 Liaoning plugin exception flood, PLA AEP SubAmmunition, MissileControl and others) add per active unit? Compare the same large mission with BepInEx code mods enabled and disabled.
What does the [PlottingTable] Payload hold (it is 95% or more of every mission save and could not be decoded here)? Does it grow without bound over a long persistent session?

Are terrain height and collision, ship grounding and submarine terrain avoidance computed correctly for units far from the camera's loaded chunks (ChunksViewDistance=4)? Do AI ships find long sea routes on their own (for example Brest to the Mediterranean via Gibraltar)?

Why did the player make the 'SULU SEA OFFENSIVE smaller / much smaller / v2 / v3' variants? Was it performance, or design? Ask the player, because it is the only possible user-side size signal and it is undocumented.
